messages:
incident-bot: PAGER - P0: spike in 5xx/gateway errors across v1 inference gateway (svc: api-gateway), multiple customers reporting timeouts. Notifying on-call @maya. https://alerts.redwood/in/INC-2469123456 :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): I'm up. seeing a sustained bump in 502/504s since ~2469123400, error rate ~9% over last 5m. traces show gateway timeouts hitting backend 'prefix-cache-proxy'.

liam (sre): copying logs -> `kubectl logs -n prod prefix-cache-proxy --tail=200 | grep ERROR | head` shows repeated eviction errors and reconnects to kv-store. Might be an eviction storm.

anika (runtime): the runtime is also throwing "kv: unexpected checksum" in a few traces. Could be corruption surfacing when prefix cache lookup fails during heavy churn.

maya (oncall): customer impact: a handful of high-traffic tenants seeing increased request latencies and 502s, CS flagged two paid customers. Samir - can you message affected customers that we're investigating and put a short ETA?

samir (cs): will ping them now with the standard ETA note. telling them 30 min while we triage.

ops-bot: deployed alert: pref-cache-eviction-rate > 500/min for 3m. Autoscaler not triggered because this is cache-level.

liam (sre): quick mitigation proposals (ranked):
1) Flip prefix cache read-through to bypass mode for contention-heavy shards (fast but increases backend QPS).
2) Add short-term 10s retry+backoff at gateway to reduce immediate 5xx waterfall.
3) Scale up kv-store read replicas and increase connection pool.

anika (runtime): I can flip bypass for a subset of hot shards (shard IDs in the last 10m) and enable a temporary circuit-breaker to stop retry storms. Doing a canary: shard 137, 142.

maya (oncall): do it. record commands and keep small blast radius.

anika (runtime): rolling command:```bash
# disable prefix read for shard 137 and 142
redwoodctl config set prefix_cache.read_enabled=false --shard=137
redwoodctl config set prefix_cache.read_enabled=false --shard=142
```
Applying canary now.

liam (sre): creating a short-lived traffic rule to send 10% of gateway traffic for those customers to backup model instances in another pool, so we can see if errors drop without taking whole fleet offline.

maya (oncall): update: after toggling read bypass on shards 137/142, 5xx for those shards dropped to ~0.8% within 90s. Overall cluster error rate down from 9% -> 4.5%.

anika (runtime): logs show the eviction spikes correspond to an unusually high TTL expiration event on several prefix segments. Metric query: `sum(evictions_total{component="prefix_cache"}) by (shard)` -> shows shards 137/142/198 in top 5.

liam (sre): suspect root cause: a background compaction job for the kv-store deferred TTL updates, causing many keys to become eligible simultaneously -> eviction surge -> cache miss storm -> gateway timeouts.

eve (prod-eng): timeline note: compaction job was kicked at 2469123300 as part of nightly maintenance but a retry loop got stuck and retriggered multiple times during high traffic window. We need to change compaction to rate-limit.

maya (oncall): next mitigation: disable/slow compaction and keep prefix read bypass for additional shards while we stabilize. liam, can you adjust kv-store compaction throttle?

liam (sre): throttling compaction now:```sql
UPDATE system_jobs SET rate_limit = 0.1 WHERE job_type = 'compaction';
```
Slowing it to 10% of normal. Monitoring effect.

maya (oncall): metrics: eviction rate dropped 85% after throttle. Gateway 5xx down to 1.2% cluster-wide. Customer reports still some errors but improving. Samir - relay update.

samir (cs): customers acknowledged. one asked for a postmortem, ticket created: PM-7892.

anika (runtime): quick follow-ups planned:
- Add a guard that staggers TTL expirations across a window to avoid mass eligible keys.
- Add checksum validation during async compaction to catch corruption earlier.

liam (sre): permanent fixes:
- Respect QPS-aware compaction scheduling (don't compaction when shard QPS > threshold).
- Add per-shard eviction dampening to spread evictions across seconds.

maya (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall (liam):
- State: prefix eviction storm caused transient 5xx; immediate mitigations applied: prefix read bypass (select shards), compaction throttled.
- Actions remaining: roll out bypass to remaining hot shards gradually (keep under 20% traffic reroute), implement TTL staggering and compaction rate change in config PR, follow up with CS on PM-7892.

liam (sre): taking handoff. I'll keep the throttled compaction and monitor for 2 hours, then plan controlled full rollout of bypass if necessary.

eve (prod-eng): creating an RFC to change compaction behavior and add circuit-breaker semantics: https://go.redwood/rfc/compaction-backpressure.

anika (runtime): putting a short-lived dashboard link with key graphs: https://grafana.redwood/d/prefix-evictions?orgId=1&from=2469123300&to=2469123700

maya (oncall): closing pager for now, setting status to "mitigated". Will keep monitoring for 1h before clear. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED - INC-2469123456 set to status=mitigated by maya. Handoff to liam for watch.

liam (sre): final note to handoff: ensure we capture exact compaction job logs and correlate with traffic spikes; attach to postmortem.

samir (cs): will coordinate PM and affected-customer outreach.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll add a short runbook snippet for eviction-storm mitigation to the oncall handbook. :pray:

end of thread
